name: Rufus (son of Simon of Cyrene)
title: The chosen one in the Lord
summary: Rufus was the son of Simon of Cyrene, the man who was forced to carry Jesus' cross on the way to Golgotha. He is mentioned by Paul in Romans as 'the chosen one in the Lord', suggesting he was a prominent Christian in the church at Rome. His mother is also warmly referred to by Paul as a mother to him as well.

keyEvents.title: The Father's Carrying of the Cross
keyEvents.description: Rufus' father, Simon of Cyrene, was forced by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus' cross to Golgotha. Mark identifies Simon as the father of Alexander and Rufus, suggesting that the sons were known to early Christians.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Greeting to Rufus
keyEvents.description: Paul sends a special greeting to Rufus in his letter to the church at Rome, calling him 'the chosen one in the Lord'. This indicates that Rufus held a prominent position in the church.

keyEvents.title: His Mother's Care for Paul
keyEvents.description: Paul refers to Rufus' mother as also being his own mother, showing that she had shown him maternal care and hospitality at some point during his ministry.
